claims.text: The target material is a single-phase, compositionally disordered high-entropy-alloy solid solution containing multiple principal elements.
A predictive model combining ab initio phonon-dispersion calculations with machine learning can represent local lattice distortions and disorder effects.
Local lattice distortions enhance phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Mass fluctuations enhance phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Enhanced phonon scattering from local distortions and mass fluctuations lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
Including multiscale configurational-disorder information enables the model to account for distortion-induced phonon scattering.
Accounting explicitly for distortion-induced phonon scattering produces more realistic predictions of thermal transport.
The proposed approach will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional single-parameter or averaged-alloy models.
The proposed approach will reduce phonon-thermal-conductivity prediction error by approximately 15–20% relative to conventional methods that omit detailed disorder effects.
The intended temperature range is 300–600 K.
The approach is intended for alloys that remain homogeneous and do not undergo significant phase segregation during testing.
The model is applicable only to homogeneous, well-mixed high-entropy alloys.
The model's advantage may diminish or reverse in alloys undergoing elemental segregation or phase separation.
The model's advantage may diminish or reverse when anharmonic effects dominate thermal transport.
The magnitude of the prediction improvement may depend on alloy composition and temperature.
The model's robustness to slight microstructural inhomogeneity is not established.
The hypothesis is falsified if, for homogeneous alloys tested from 300 to 600 K, the proposed model does not reduce prediction error by at least 10% relative to conventional models.
Improved prediction accuracy in significantly phase-segregated alloys is specified as a falsifying result for the claimed applicability boundary.

contradictions.description: The boundary says performance outside homogeneous alloys may merely diminish or reverse, whereas the falsification rule treats any improved accuracy in phase-segregated alloys as falsifying. Improvement outside the intended domain does not necessarily contradict the softer claim that the advantage may diminish, so the boundary and falsification criterion are not fully aligned.
